title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: share files from iPhone and iPad apps to start a Copilot Chat
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts match the roadmap, and Microsoft documentation supports the licensing, account protections and organisational access control. Targeted searches confirmed the narrower documentation gaps about the iOS sharing route; the page appropriately asks administrators to test its account and policy behaviour.

claims.claim: The blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. Select the Available Apps list. Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. Select Block app.

claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps controls are available only to Global Admins.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant control over organisational Copilot Chat access, including licensed users and the mobile app.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users. This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.claim: Blocked users see the Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization screen.
claims.quote: Users blocked through Integrated Apps see the Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization experience when opening Copilot Chat in the Copilot app.

claims.claim: The organisational Integrated Apps block is not the documented control for personal Microsoft-account access.
claims.quote: IT admins of work or school environments can limit their users from accessing the Copilot app with their Microsoft account (personal account) by using Tenant Restrictions.
